bug_info.bug_desc: In the pre-merge code, the EDN synchronizer's req_chk_i input was tied only to the synchronized life-cycle escalation signal. As a result, when a fatal alert was asserted and the AES core dropped an outstanding EDN request before receiving the EDN acknowledgement, the synchronizer's request-checking logic could treat this as a handshake protocol violation. The spec explicitly permits a pending entropy request to be dropped when a fatal alert or life-cycle escalation is active, so the old gating condition was too restrictive and did not cover the fatal-alert case.
bug_info.fix_hint: Create a separate request-check enable signal that is deasserted both when life-cycle escalation is active and when the fatal alert is asserted, then feed this signal to the EDN synchronizer's req_chk_i port. This allows the EDN request to be dropped before acknowledgement in the fatal-alert/escalation case, which is acceptable because the module must be reset before normal operation resumes.
